<reason>A wins by distinguishing a necessary condition for sale from permission or immunity to sell. It directly answers the stalking hypothetical and establishes a surviving benefit: unauthorized sales become unlawful without individuals having to prove malicious use. B raises meaningful concerns about manipulated consent, but repeatedly mistakes incomplete protection for affirmative legalization. Its eventual blanket-minimization proposal undercuts its earlier useful-data objection and remains compatible with A’s minimum restriction. The speculative claim that consent regulation would crowd out stronger protections does not establish a persuasive disadvantage.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s questions forced B to concede that consent overrides no use ban and that its alternative would prevent every precise-location sale. A then crystallized the decisive response: stronger prohibitions do not refute this minimum, and imperfect consent does not erase protection for people who never authorize a sale.</best_rebuttal>
